findings.assessment: Exact implicit representation is potentially faithful; actual consumer and decoder are not demonstrated.
findings.detail: The actual consumer is the component expected to use the indexed energy, not an omniscient observer, arbitrary test harness or producer with unavailable state. No named physical component, retained state inventory, concrete interface or decoder is supplied. This is permissible at source-review stage and prevents RI eligibility claims. AS PS does not prescribe a literal numeral, stored counter, integer format or API. An exact decoder must map the actual consumer state, response and genuinely available context to a unique accepted ordinal and reset sequence for every event. All-zero/restart, invalid-attempt and finite-wrap witnesses refute observer/transaction/attempt/modular shortcuts. Supported lifetime is not authority to introduce a finite epoch or restart exemption.
findings.AS_impact: Class b representation clarification; class d physical evidence remains due. Observer-only indexing, finite epochs, forced resets, exhaustion or narrowed restart support would be class c material changes requiring new delegated amendment.
findings.followup: Identify consumer, actual state/context, accepted-event/result bijection, exact decoder, reset association, arbitrary-rank argument and full cost/ownership before physical eligibility; no service presumed.

findings.assessment: Persistent logical result debt is source-consistent; universal failure survival or physical exactly-once delivery is not established.
findings.detail: D001 requires one exact indexed result per accepted valid event. Acceptance, commit and publication are distinct; losing a result or reporting a fault cannot turn an unfulfilled obligation into a fulfilled one. Reset/restart does not retrospectively unaccept the event. The absence of a crash model and S25 no-universal-recovery disclaimer mean this is a preservation rule, not guaranteed recovery from arbitrary information destruction, permanent disconnection or permanent stalls. The debt can remain outstanding and conformity unestablished. Exactly one logical result does not forbid retransmitting the same result under a reviewed protocol; it does not provide reliable exactly-once transport or acknowledgment. A new guarantee of recovery/availability across specified failures would require explicit delegated amendment and failure assumptions.
findings.AS_impact: Class a per-event output/invalid invariance; class b explicit debt interpretation; class d acceptance/delivery/fault models. No new universal failure guarantee follows from R2 read with its express limitation.
findings.followup: In later delegated lifecycle disposition distinguish preserved obligation from a new guarantee of recovery, define supported failures and retry identity, then supply capacity/retention evidence. No rollback, fault-report discharge, invalid padding or replay as new acceptance.

findings.assessment: The unconditional reset-acknowledgment wording is not established as a necessary consequence of accepted requirements.
findings.detail: S28 (lines 67-69) says the contract must identify reset order AND acknowledgment at the consumer boundary. Correct reset ordering and old/new non-aliasing are necessary; a distinct acknowledgment obligation is not present in D001 Q4/Q6 or the activated AS. Stage-7 and the bounded D003 disposition explicitly leave acknowledgment and reset completion unselected. A logical interface could establish order and association through an ordered reset marker and ordered results, with the consumer tracking that order, without a separate acknowledgment event. That is a countermodel to necessity, not approval or evidence that such a mechanism is available here. As written, S28 does not say acknowledgment may be absent when equivalent order/association is proved. A literal mandatory acknowledgment imposes an additional observable/protocol restriction, contrary to the unqualified no-D001-amendment/semantics-only framing. If acknowledgment merely names any way the consumer knows reset association, the text must say so rather than relying on reviewer repair.
findings.AS_impact: Reset order/non-aliasing class b; later evidence class d; a required positive acknowledgment event/service is class c and needs a new explicit delegated amendment. Current bounded authorization for clarification does not activate it.
findings.followup: Revise the exact source to distinguish required observable ordering/association from an optional acknowledgment mechanism, or explicitly seek a new delegated amendment adopting the extra acknowledgment obligation with assumptions and consequences. Do not activate this exact text as an unqualified clarification.

findings.assessment: Acceptance, finite capacity, reset completion and restart association remain unresolved interface questions.
findings.detail: The physical acceptance event can be reviewed prospectively but cannot silently exclude valid ordered samples to make capacity work. S13/S14/S33/S40 retain that constraint. Q+1 pending entries exceed Q slots under the explicit no-other-retention assumptions; numeric tail does not retain arbitrary unpaid history. Arbitrarily long finite stalls need justified storage or lossless coordination. Permanent unavailability cannot satisfy eventual delivery, although no finite deadline or reset-completion bound is imposed. Draining under an indefinite stall may never complete; preserving old identity needs retained state/association and safe reuse. Neither a publisher pause facility, a reliable acknowledgment service nor crash-safe storage can be presumed.
findings.AS_impact: No present authority for new valid-event restrictions, supported-lifetime caps or mandatory flow control. New guarantees or operating restrictions are class c amendments; mechanisms preserving agreed observables remain class d.
findings.followup: Keep actual acceptance/delivery/reset linearization, consumer information lifetime, retry/deduplication, retention, service/failure assumptions and attributable resources open for independently authorized work. No concrete protocol is authored here.

findings.assessment: Numeric requirements, adopted model, F, proof scope and open obligations are preserved at source level.
findings.detail: The latest-32 exact PS, startup/reset zero padding, accepted order and invalid rejection remain unchanged. Domain 0..4095, nominal-only 1 ms, hypothetical 32-bit/no-FPU model and 2048-byte detector-attributable RAM remain governing. Owned persistent/scratch/stack plus index, transaction, queues and shared-attributable storage count. Exclusive upstream ownership requires evidence and does not mean zero device energy.
